title: Hierholzer undirected sufficiency — even-degree connected graph has an Eulerian circuit

problemStatement.formal: G \text{ connected} \ \wedge\ (\forall v,\ \deg(v)\text{ even}) \ \Longrightarrow\ \exists\ \text{Eulerian circuit in } G.
problemStatement.plain: The famous Königsberg-bridges result has an easy necessity direction (an Eulerian circuit forces all degrees even). This problem is the harder **sufficiency** direction via Hierholzer's algorithm: if a connected graph has all even degrees, you can actually build a single closed tour using every edge once by splicing together cycles.

insights: Target is undirected Hierholzer SUFFICIENCY: connected + all-even-degree implies an Eulerian circuit exists. Necessity is already proved in KonigsbergOQ02OQ01OQ02.lean (eulerian_circuit_forall_even).

A fully-proved DIRECTED analogue exists in KonigsbergOQ02OQ01.lean (directed_euler_circuit_sufficient_corrected, 0 sorries, ~900 lines) with reusable machinery: splice constructor, removeArcList (arc removal preserving balance), and maximal_balanced_trail_is_circuit. This is a strong structural template for the undirected argument.

KEY INSIGHT (reduction failure): the naive reduction replacing each undirected edge {u,v} with two directed arcs (u,v),(v,u) yields a balanced strongly-connected digraph, so the directed theorem gives a directed Eulerian circuit -- but that circuit traverses each undirected edge TWICE (once per direction). It is therefore NOT an undirected Eulerian circuit. A native undirected Hierholzer argument is required.

The undirected parity invariant is Even (G.degree v) (from Mathlib IsEulerian.even_degree_iff / card_odd_degree) rather than the directed inDegree=outDegree balance, because undirected incidence is symmetric.

IsEulerian is defined in Mathlib as (∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, p.edges.count e = 1) — NOT (IsTrail ∧ covers all edges). Trail-ness is a DERIVED consequence (IsEulerian.isTrail). The construction invariant to maintain is therefore the per-edge count=1 condition; this corrects the earlier plan framing.

Confirmed (web search + local check): Mathlib4 Trails module has only the necessity/property lemmas (IsEulerian.even_degree_iff, IsEulerian.card_odd_degree). No Eulerian existence/Hierholzer construction exists upstream, so sufficiency must be built natively.

The directed Digraph proof in KonigsbergOQ02OQ01.lean is NOT reusable: it is built on a bespoke Digraph structure with its own Walk/splice/removeArcList/arcCount — none are SimpleGraph.Walk objects. A native SimpleGraph mirror is required.

BREAKTHROUGH (extremal collapse): a MAXIMUM-length trail (length bounded by edgeFinset.card, L1) is (Step1) edge-maximal at its endpoint — else concat an unused incident edge = longer trail (nodup_concat + length_concat) — hence CLOSED via verified eq_of_isTrail_edgeMaximal; and (Step2) EULERIAN — else an unused edge incident to a support vertex, rotate-to-it + concat = longer trail. This needs NO induction on edgeFinset.card, NO residual graph, and does NOT use Sub-lemma B at all (B stays verified but off critical path).

KEY: the boundary-crossing step (find an unused edge incident to a visited vertex) is ALREADY in Mathlib as Walk.exists_boundary_dart (Walks/Basic.lean:388): a walk from u∈S to a∉S has a dart d with d.fst∈S, d.snd∉S. Combined with snd_mem_support_of_mem_edges (a used edge's far endpoint is in support) it forces d.edge unused & incident to S. No custom 'S closed under adjacency' lemma needed.

Rotation preserves everything needed BUT via IsRotated (~r), not Perm (~): Walk.rotate (WalkDecomp:273) re-bases a closed walk at any support vertex; IsTrail.rotate (Paths:495) keeps it a trail; rotate_edges (WalkDecomp:294) gives (rotate).edges ~r edges. Unused-ness transports by IsRotated.mem_iff (Rotate.lean:403); length by .perm→List.Perm.length_eq (IsRotated.perm, Rotate.lean:397). (Session 6 CORRECTION: an earlier note wrongly said Perm.mem_iff/Perm.length_eq directly — rotate_edges is ~r; Mathlib's own Paths.lean:497 uses (rotate_edges h).perm.nodup_iff.)

Arbitrary-edge decomposition ∃ a b, e = s(a,b) is Sym2.exists.mp ⟨e, rfl⟩ (Sym2.«exists», Sym2.lean:155) — NOT Sym2.other_spec' (which needs a membership proof). For an edge KNOWN incident to v (v ∈ e), use Sym2.Mem.other hvE + Sym2.other_spec (Sym2.lean:353,357), noncomputable but fine in a Prop goal.

Not-Eulerian ⇒ unused edge is clean: IsTrail ⇒ edges Nodup ⇒ count ≤ 1 (List.nodup_iff_count_le_one); the Eulerian requirement count=1 fails only if count=0, i.e. edge unused (List.count_pos_iff). No degree/parity argument needed for this direction.

Mathlib has only the DECOMPOSITION direction for trails under append (IsTrail.of_append_left/of_append_right); the CONSTRUCTION direction (disjoint-edge trails concatenate to a trail) and the splice are absent and were built natively.
Splice needs [DecidableEq V] because takeUntil/dropUntil/rotate require it; isTrail_append does not.

rotate_edges gives (d.rotate h).edges ~r d.edges (List.IsRotated), so .mem_iff transports edge membership — lets a residual circuit rooted anywhere be re-based at the shared vertex without changing its edge set.

Connectivity glue for Hierholzer: if a closed trail's support were closed under adjacency (every incident edge used), connectivity forces support=V, so any missing edge would be incident and hence used — contradiction. Formalized as exists_boundary_edge_of_missing. Generic helper forall_of_adjClosed (adjacency-closed predicate + connected + witness ⟹ holds everywhere) is reusable.

Sub-lemma D disconnection BUG + fix (r5 Session 4): recursing the sufficiency IH into H=G.deleteEdges c.edges is unsound because H is generally disconnected. Correct Hierholzer assembly: strong induction on m(c)=G.edgeFinset.card - c.edges.length (missed edges) over closed trails c in the FIXED connected G. Step: bridge gives unused edge s(w,x), w in c.support; deg_H(w)>=2 (edge survives + B evenness); take a MAXIMAL trail from w in H — nonempty (deg>0) and closed (A applied to H) — as residual d; transport d:H.Walk to G.Walk via Walk.mapLe (deleteEdges_le); splice (exists_isTrail_splice_of_mem_support) gives c' with edges c.edges⊍d.edges, m decreases; IH. Connectivity is used ONLY via the bridge, never re-required of H.
